title: The Whistler
paragraphs: A dark crime anthology narrated by the all-knowing Whistler, whose stories often follow ordinary people into murder, greed, or deception before ending with irony or unexpected justice.

CBS mystery/crime anthology whose recurring Whistler narrator frames self-contained stories. The current 2026 specialist project distinguishes the West Coast, Eastern spurs, military/syndicated copies, and the final East-only broadcasts.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: Early sustaining West Coast era (May 16, 1942 to December 18, 1943) on [[org|org.5d1a575385a05456|CBS Pacific Network]], Signal Oil West Coast era (December 19, 1943 to October 17, 1954) on [[org|org.5d1a575385a05456|CBS Pacific Network]], and Final split national era (February 27, 1955 to September 22, 1955) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Wilbur Hatch (music, composer, and conductor), George W. Allen (producer, director, and production), Marvin Miller (announcer, performer, and music), Bill Forman (performer, announcer, and narrator), Joel Malone (writer and producer), Betty Lou Gerson (performer), and Harold Swanton (writer and director).

Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.5d1a575385a05456|CBS Pacific Network]], [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]], [[org|org.4798d1172deaae2c|Armed Forces Radio Service]], [[org|org.cd82fd99edb39caa|Armed Forces Radio and Television Service]], and [[org|org.244a08401c2c9142|WRVR-FM]].

The stories often return to Murder and attempted murder, Greed and financial motive, Blackmail and coercion, Deception and concealed identity, Theft and robbery, and Insurance and inheritance schemes.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes West Coast regional network success, Signal Oil regional sponsorship, Radio-to-film noir franchise, and Radio mystery during the television transition.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]], [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]], [[show|escape|Escape]], [[show|screen-directors-playhouse|Screen Directors Playhouse]], and [[show|broadway-is-my-beat|Broadway Is My Beat]].
